section: A38 rehearsal — rollback floor re-run against the merged fix — 2026-09-08
headline: On a seeded stack with real transcoded media, deploy/rollback.sh completed an app-only rollback across an additive migration: the previous release's migrator met a newer CLEAN ledger, logged the no-op line and exited 0, and the old binaries served the newer schema completely. Rolling back to a release WITHOUT the fix still fails in the migration one-shot, and now fails loudly with the trailer instead of dying under set -e.

lab.shape: one disposable compose project -p a38b on an arm64 macOS host; api 18080, frontend 13000, Caddy on 80/443, VIDRA_TLS_MODE=plain-http, STORAGE_BACKEND=local, bundled Postgres 18 + Redis 8
lab.meta_checkout: throwaway clone of this repo with its own nested vidra-core / vidra-search / vidra-user clones, so deploy.sh's checkout pinning (AGENTS.md rule 3) was real; the architect's checkouts were never touched
lab.registry: local OCI registry on 127.0.0.1:5001 served through VIDRA_IMAGE_REGISTRY (every prod service carries pull_policy: always)

lab_deviations: RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false and REGISTRATION_ENABLED=true in the lab env file so a synthetic seeder could create three accounts and poll an upload; neither is a supported production posture and neither touches the paths under test

verbatim.sc2_migrator_noop: {"level":"WARN","msg":"schema version 136 is newer than this binary's newest migration 135; nothing to apply","ledger_version":136,"embedded_max":135,"dirty":false}
verbatim.sc3_migrator_failure: dbmigrate: apply migrations: no migration found for version 136: read down for version 136 .: file does not exist
verbatim.sc3_trailer:
[rollback] THE ROLLBACK TARGET IS ALSO UNHEALTHY.
  compose up -d exited non-zero; its output is above. Check the migration one-shots FIRST: '... logs migrate search-migrate'. A message like 'no migration found for version N' means this release's migrator is older than the schema in front of it — the app itself is fine on that schema, but the one-shot has to exit 0 before api, search and frontend are allowed to start.

  If the newer release ran an incompatible migration, the old code cannot read the new schema — restore the pre-deploy dump before rolling back again:
      ./deploy/restore.sh backups/pre-deploy-<ts>.dump.gz
verbatim.restore_not_checked: [restore] core: the pinned image (VIDRA_CORE_TAG=v0.6.2-arm64) does not answer 'migrate embedded-max', so the dump's schema 135 could NOT be checked against it. Every release cut before that subcommand existed lands here. Continuing — but if the migrator step below refuses the restored database, this pairing is the first thing to look at.
verbatim.restore_matched: [restore] core: dump schema 135 matches what VIDRA_CORE_TAG=v0.6.3-a37 carries — nothing to apply.
verbatim.restore_dirty_refusal: [restore] ERROR: core: the dump's schema_migrations ledger is DIRTY at version 136 — a migration was half-applied when it was taken, and both migrators refuse a dirty ledger. ... Nothing was changed.
verbatim.restore_lowmig_refusal: [restore] ERROR: core: the dump is at 135; pinned VIDRA_CORE_TAG=v0.6.3-a37lowmig carries up to 130. ... Nothing was changed.
verbatim.doctor_dirty: ✗ schema ledger: the core migration ledger (schema_migrations) is DIRTY at version 136: a migration failed halfway and the schema state is unknown
verbatim.doctor_ledger_ahead: ✓ schema ledger: the core migration ledger (schema_migrations) is at version 136 and clean
verbatim.force_refusal_without_flag: refusing to force schema_migrations to version 135: this rewrites the ledger WITHOUT running any migration SQL, so the schema must already match. Re-run with --yes-i-know if that is true
verbatim.force_applied: before: version=136 dirty=true / after: version=135 dirty=false

findings.text: vidra doctor cannot say 'your binary is behind the schema'. On the rolled-back stack it printed a green ✓ naming version 136 and clean — truthful about the ledger, silent about the one fact that distinguishes this state from a matched deployment. It has both numbers available now that migrate embedded-max exists.

A rollback.sh refusal after the env rewrite leaves the env rewritten. Runs 7 and an unknown-tag attempt died after set_key had pinned the target tags, and the pull message reads '($ENV_FILE restored from ${ENV_FILE}.bak if you need to undo)', which can be read as a statement that it was restored. It was not; the config -q failure path a few lines above does restore it.
Re-confirms A37-3: restore.sh stops api, search and frontend before the schema preflight, so both new refusals (runs 13 and 16) took the site down and then correctly changed nothing.

An api-only outage behind Caddy hangs rather than errors: lb_try_duration 30s holds requests instead of 502ing, so a probe with a 5 s timeout reports a connection failure while a browser simply waits.

release_note_facts_v063: An app-only rollback across an additive migration now works, from v0.6.3 onward — proven on a running stack.
Rolling back to v0.6.2 or older requires the restore path; rollback.sh now names that failure instead of dying silently.

A restore's pinned tags are part of the restore: restore.sh refuses, before the drop, a dump the pinned images cannot reach and a dump whose ledger is dirty; against a release predating migrate embedded-max it reports NOT CHECKED and continues.

Carried forward: access tokens 401 once after a roll-forward and it is one-way; process_heartbeats is populated only by the new release; new env defaults apply only when set; the deploy floor refuses a non-semver tag.

gates.bash -n: clean on deploy/*.sh, tests/*.sh, install.sh, bootstrap.sh
gates.shellcheck: 0.11.0 -x -S warning clean on the same set
gates.prod render: --profile core --profile frontend: postgres, redis, search, search-migrate, migrate and prep-volumes publish no ports; api 127.0.0.1:8080, frontend 127.0.0.1:3000

unverified: The RELEASED amd64 v0.6.2 images were never run on this arm64 host; 'rolling back to v0.6.2 fails' is proven against the v0.6.2 source tree rebuilt for this architecture
Only the core ledger moved; search stayed at 18, so a rollback across a search migration is untested at the stack level

External Postgres and external Redis; the bundle path (expected_version from vidra-bundle.manifest); acme / internal / external TLS modes; multi-replica and split api/worker topologies; a rollback across more than one release; S3 storage (verify-blobs ran only against the local media volume); restore.sh --allow-schema-mismatch against a live stack
teardown: the -p a38b project and its volumes, the local registry and its volume, the three images built for this run (v0.6.4-a38, v0.6.4-a38bad, v0.6.2-arm64) and the throwaway meta clone with its nested checkouts were all removed; the four A37 images are kept
